bugs.text: The stage never advances. updateEnemies sets allEntered=false whenever the enemies array is empty, and the stage-clear test at 545 requires allEntered, so after the 40th kill the game sits on an empty screen forever (no enemies, no dives, Enter does nothing outside the title). Every feature beyond stage 1 (tractor beam gated by stage>=2 at 287, capture, dual fighter, challenging stages, stage scaling, extra ship, more than one badge) is unreachable.

`chalBonus` is never declared; under 'use strict' the assignment at 529 (end of a challenging stage) throws a ReferenceError inside frame(), so requestAnimationFrame is never re-armed and the whole game freezes. Masked only because stage 3 cannot be reached.

Every enemy still on its entry path fires an aimed shot with probability 0.004 per tick (roughly 20 enemies in flight at once, about 5 aimed bullets per second, speed 1.8) before the player has shot anything. The play-test screenshots show one reserve ship left at 5 s, none left plus an explosion at 8 s, and the title screen again by 30 s: all three ships lost during the stage-1 entry.
Dive paths are pure homing with a capped turn rate; a diver that overshoots the player turns back up toward it and can loop around or ram from below instead of sweeping off the bottom.
Entering enemies land on the raw slot then snap to the swayed formation position (up to 12 px jump); sway amplitude snaps from 12 to 4 when the last enemy lands; breath is never reset between stages.
Killing a diving Boss also destroys its Goei escorts and pays 160 each; in the arcade the escorts survive.
A tractor-beam capture would play the player-explosion burst and death sound, and the ship is drawn in normal colours (not red) while being pulled up (unreachable in this build).
sDie (enemy destroyed) is defined but never called; enemy hit and enemy destroyed share the same noise burst.
Pressing M while a tractor beam is sounding does not stop the running oscillator; mute only prevents new sounds.
Stage-badge table includes a 70 denomination that the arcade does not have.
Extra ship test is `score>nextExtra`, so landing on exactly 20,000 does not award until the next point.

summary: The file is compact and well organised in outline (state, update, render, fixed-step loop all cleanly separated) and most of the Galaga vocabulary is present in code: pixel-string sprites with two frames per enemy, Bezier group entries, sway and breathing, escorted boss dives, correct point tables, a tractor beam with capture, rescue, dual fighter, captive fire, challenging stages, HUD, results screen and a full set of synthesized sounds. But what a player actually gets is one stage of Galaga and then a dead screen: a single inverted condition (allEntered is false once the array is empty) makes stage 1 unclearable, and since the beam is gated on stage 2, the signature mechanic, the challenging stage and all later-stage behaviour can never be seen. Stage 1 itself is punishing rather than faithful: entering enemies pour aimed shots at the player and divers home continuously instead of flying patterns, and the play-test lost all three ships before the formation had finished arriving. Readability suffers from extremely long one-line statements, there is dead code and an undeclared variable that would crash under strict mode, and the challenging-stage counters are never incremented. It looks like Galaga at a glance and is built on the right ideas, but it is not a working game past its first wave.
